teaching_reason: The student should understand scapular vascularization as a regional network supplying muscles, periosteum and adjacent osseous regions rather than memorizing one isolated artery as the universal nutrient vessel of the scapula.
context: Scapular peri-osseous and intraosseous multi-source arterial supply.

teaching_reason: The glenoid is not only a bony articular surface; the region must be mentally connected with the sensory innervation of the joint capsule and the nerves that travel around the shoulder.
context: Proprioceptive and nociceptive sensory innervation of the glenohumeral joint.

teaching_reason: The same nerve that is topographically important at the scapular notch also has functional relevance to the posterior shoulder and articular region.
context: Suprascapular nerve articular branching before and after notch traversal.

teaching_reason: The acromion should be taught not as a perfectly invariant process but as a region with developmental and morphologic variation relevant to specimen and imaging interpretation.
context: Acromial morphotypes (I-III) and developmental non-fusion (os acromiale).

teaching_reason: A normally ligament-bridged notch can present a different osseous configuration when the ligament ossifies, directly linking variation anatomy with topographic nerve passage.
context: Suprascapular notch bony roof conversion and entrapment risk.
